dispositions.method: Round three of 1793. On 11 November 2026 the owner set the rule 'every story alike': a reviewed story is described by what kind of text it is and whose account, in the papers' own words, never as what happened; sensitive subjects get no special treatment. Items that earlier rounds held back for framing are therefore counted by the year's own rule, exactly like any other item: what reaches it is admitted, what does not stays out. As before, an excerpt ends before the names of private people where it can, and stories that turn on private people stay out. The items rounds one and two left out for framing were read again with phrase searches over all 1,751 pages of 1793 in both transcriptions (phrase_patterns_round3.json, phrase_hits_round3.json), every hit was read, the papers in print without a hit were searched with loose keywords (no missed printing), and every admitted printing was checked against its page scan by AI reviewers (scan_batches/batch_09.json and batch_10.json, SCAN_PROTOCOL.md, scan_points_round3.json).
dispositions.selection_rule: For 1793 a story needs one printed item found in 6 or more newspapers, counted item by item, the two titles of a renamed paper once (the owner's decision of 10 November 2026). Where several items belong to one affair, each is its own group under a parent story; a sub-story may have fewer papers than the threshold when its parent reaches it. As for the 4-paper documents of Dumouriez's defection in round one, items in 4 papers are not admitted as sub-stories.

counted_item_by_item.The War Office paragraph: 6 papers (NGz 4 September, GUS 7 September, PG 16 September, NHG and AHL 17 September, CI 25 September). Two other items on the commissioners are in 3 papers each and not part of the group: their letter from the mouth of Detroit river (GUS, PG, AHL twice) and a paragraph on the nations' answer of 2 August (NGz, PG, CI).
counted_item_by_item.The German Creek letter: 6 papers (NGz and GUS 11 September, PG 16 September, NHG and AHL 24 September, CI 2 October); PG prints it from a Georgetown paper of 7 September.
counted_item_by_item.Cap Français: Captain Fanning's account (New York, 9 July; NGz 10 July, NHG and AHL 16 July, MIR and PG 22 July, GUS on the issue filed under 23 July, which is of 13 July: 6 papers) and the brig Mary's passengers' report (GUS 27 July, NGz 31 July, PG 5 August, NHG and AHL 6 August, CI 14 August: 6 papers) are two items about the same days; each reaches the threshold and each is its own group under the parent 'News from Cap Français, June 1793'.

not_admitted.The civil commissioners' proclamation of: 4 papers (NGz and GUS 27 July, NHG and AHL 13 August; NGz quotes it again in a commentary of 21 August): below the threshold, and not a sub-story, as for the 4-paper documents of Dumouriez's defection.
not_admitted.The letter of Polverel and Sonthonax to: 4 papers (GUS 29 May, NGz 1 June, AHL 18 June, MIR 24 June): below the threshold.
not_admitted.The Fugitive Slave Act: 'An act respecting fugitives from justice, and persons escaping from the service of their masters': its text is in 2 papers (MIR 11 March, GUS 17 April); its title is also in the lists of the session's acts (NGz 6 March, GUS 9 March, KG 13 April), which are a different item. Below the threshold.
not_admitted.Private people (5 papers each): The prosecutions of the seamen Singleterry and Henfield, and a killing near Middletown, New Jersey: below the threshold, and stories that turn on private people stay out.
